When I was younger my weight fluctuated a lot. My mother always been obese (she said since she had me and would often remind me that it was my fault) My older sister by 11 months was always bigger but I believe was officially obese by 10 years old, and my father became disabled after slipping on a piece of toilet paper while obese and has been living off the system ever since. Because of them(and most of the community around me) It never dawned on me that I was overweight.

When I hit about 12 years old I was already have problems related to my weight(arthritis, stomach/ digestive trouble, breathing, anemia) even though I hadn't hit obesity yet, and the doctor made it clear that I needed to drop weight to feel better. This hurt my feelings of course but I wanted to do what he said. Over the next few years I tried to lose weight, not really knowing how with no internet access, not a single person in my life telling me about CICO and no choice in the foods that were brought into the house. But you better believe I heard all about starvation mode, metabolism, low fat diets, how drinks couldn’t affect weight, thyroid problems, how wanting to skip meals meant you were anorexic and how any weight lost would probably just come back anyway.

My mom would make fun of me for exercising, threaten to put me in a hospital for an eating disorder when I tried and would call me a piglet when I didn’t. At 15 I reached over 200 pounds standing at 5’, my sister was about the same size, maybe a bit more. Luckily around that time my mom got busy with a new boyfriend and social life so I was able to take my weight into my own hands without fear. Dropped down to 105 pounds in 7 months. It’s been 10 years and I’ve pretty much stayed the same outside of pregnancy while my sister unfortunately went the other way and is now about 400 pounds.

My story is the only reason I can’t laugh at fat children/teens. For most of them they don’t even realize there’s a problem until they hit high school and then I can only imagine there are worse than my mom out there.
